h1: Hydraulic straightening presses — portal, 3-axis and sliding-table presses, 22 to 441 US tons
intro: A straightening press leaves the workpiece lying still on the bed and brings the ram to the bend: the cylinder travels along a gantry and the gantry along the bed, or the press head moves on three axes, so a long beam, a plate, a rail, a shaft or a pipe is straightened point by point without craning it under a fixed ram. NovoTech's premium line, built in Turkey, has two families, small to large: the HSPS portal (gantry) straightening presses from 110 to 441 US tons, with beds from 39.4 × 78.7″ to 59.1 × 137.8″, the cylinder travelling along the gantry on a rack drive and the gantry along the bed; and the DK-S 3-axis moving straightening presses from 220 to 441 US tons, whose cylinder moves on X, Y and Z by motorized gear drive over a 100″ bed, with a remote control as an option; and NovoTech's value line, built in China — the HP-M1 presses from 22 to 220 US tons, whose table slides out of the frame, so large and heavy parts are loaded outside the press and rolled in. Each family below has its full specification table and photos. For shafts and bar in a repair shop, a shop press with a mobile cylinder is often enough. Parts, installation and service from Mississauga, ON, Canada.

faq.a: Both leave the workpiece on the bed and move the ram to the bend. The HSPS is a gantry that runs along the bed on a rack drive, with beds to 59.1 × 137.8″ — the choice for long beams, rails and plate. The DK-S carries its cylinder on X, Y and Z over a 100″ bed with motorized gear drives, from 220 to 441 US tons, for heavy plate, beams, profiles and round bar.

It depends on the section, the material and the distance between the supports: the press has to bend the part slightly past straight. Send us the profile or the shaft diameter, the material grade, the length and how far it is out of straight, and we size the press, the bed and the supports.

faq.q: Can a shop press straighten too?
faq.a: Yes, for shafts, bar and smaller sections that can be moved under the ram. The DPM-K and DK shop presses carry the cylinder across the frame on a hand wheel, so a shaft or a frame rail stays clamped while it is straightened point by point. For beams, plate and parts too heavy or too long to move, a straightening press brings the ram to the work.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.
